title: 舍入规则对照：截断 / floor / ceil / round / 就近偶数
expected_output:
=== rounding modes compared ===
     x    (int)x   floor    ceil    round    nearbyint
    0.5        0       0       1        1           0
    1.5        1       1       2        2           2
    2.5        2       2       3        3           2
    3.5        3       3       4        4           4
   -0.5        0      -1      -0       -1          -0
   -1.5       -1      -2      -1       -2          -2
   -2.5       -2      -3      -2       -3          -2
    2.4        2       2       3        2           2
    2.6        2       2       3        3           3
   -2.6       -2      -3      -2       -3          -3

notes:
  (int) casts TRUNCATE toward zero: (int)-2.9 = -2
  IEEE default rounding is round-to-nearest TIES-TO-EVEN: 2.5 -> 2, 3.5 -> 4
  round() breaks ties AWAY FROM ZERO: 2.5 -> 3, -2.5 -> -3
  nearest-even introduces no statistical bias, which is why IEEE chose it

=== integer division rounding ===
  -7 / 2 = -3      (truncates toward zero)
  floor(-3.5) = -4   (floors toward -inf)
  ceil division trick ceil(10/3) = 4

=== tie-breaking table (why nearest-even looks strange) ===
  value   round()   nearbyint()   tie ?
    0.5       1           0         yes
    1.5       2           2         yes
    2.5       3           2         yes
    3.5       4           4         yes
  rule: on a tie keep the LAST bit even -> 2.5 -> 2 (2 is even), 3.5 -> 4 (4 is even)
